question.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(11,0.65),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{11}{x}){(0.65)}^{x}{(0.35)}^{11-x}.
$$

Computing $P(X\le 10)$ will require us to compute $f(x)$ at $x=0,1,2,3,…,10.$ However, if we compute the complement $P(X>10)$ instead, then we will only have to compute $f(x)$ at $x=11,$ which will result in a much faster computation.

Computing $P(X>10),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>10) & =P(X\in \{11\}) \\  & =f(11) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{11}{11}){(0.65)}^{11}{(0.35)}^{11-11} \\  & =1{(0.65)}^{11}{(0.35)}^{0} \\  & ≈0.009\end{aligned}
$$

 rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 10) & =1-P(X>10) \\  & ≈1-0.009 \\  & =0.991\end{aligned}
$$

 rounded to $3$ decimal places.
